## Decisions
- 2026-10-16 · **Media least privilege (S3-F4):** (1) `withMedia` has no APP_ROLE gate: the role has no BYPASSRLS and only the media container gets its URL (the api's `getDb` refuses a role without a URL). (2) `property_media` is read through a column grant on `sha256`, not whole rows: reference counts need nothing else (alt text, kinds, agency ids stay out). (3) The HMAC key, crypto keys and `WEB_URL` are not given to the media container: none of the media jobs uses them. (4) The production public-key rule is a Cloudflare WAF rule on the R2 custom domain (R2 has no per-prefix public access); MinIO's policy wildcards also match `/`, so locally the line is approximate (documented, tested).
- 2026-10-16 · **Fixture hygiene (S3-F3):** (1) Properties/media/quality suites are not purged: their reference rows carry the run id in every name, slug and key (never collide) and listings reference them (RESTRICT); only suites with fixed names (tree, catalog, staff API) clear earlier runs. (2) The Windows 0xC0000409 fork crash is documented as Windows-only (not reproducible alone or in CI's Linux runners); `verify` reruns the crashed package, CI is the gate. `verify:all` twice in a row was not attempted: each run takes ~12 min and crashes a fork on most runs on this machine.
- 2026-10-16 · **Taxonomy at scale (S3-F2):** (1) Children are cursor-paged by bytes, not capped: a client walking a 5,000-city region still gets every city. The cursor is the page number (pages are cut from an immutable tree, so no keyset is needed). (2) The reload's < 300 ms check is server execution + tree build; the dev machine's Docker Desktop transfer is logged, not asserted. (3) The staff editor reads the whole sibling set on expand (no paging): a reorder must send every sibling.
- 2026-10-16 · **Taxonomy hygiene (S3-F1):** (1) `legacy_id_maps` loses the `app_user` read now rather than moving: nothing at runtime reads it; S14 adds a STRICT tenant table for listing/contact maps. (2) "Stable queue paging": the keyset stays `(count desc, id)` — counts only grow, so a value counted again mid-browse moves above the cursor and is never shown twice (test); a snapshot cursor would hide the value instead. (3) Non-content locales are refused in the service (`VALIDATION_FAILED`), not the contract, because contracts do not depend on the i18n locale config.
- 2026-10-16 · **Bookmarks (S3-09):** (1) Folders and bookmarks are private to the member (like saved views); sharing a folder with the team is not asked for. (2) Never in Client Mode, reads included: notes are internal. (3) No FK from bookmarks to `properties`: a bookmark must survive the listing leaving the member's view (RLS) or being purged, and reads as unavailable; an own soft-deleted listing is also unavailable and cannot be bookmarked. (4) "Listing/unit": units have no table yet, so only listings are bookmarkable; unit bookmarks come with the units table (nullable `unit_id` then). (5) Caps: 100 folders per member (soft, like views), 500 bookmarks per folder (exact, folder row lock) — also the most a selection from a folder starts with (S12-04).
- 2026-10-16 · **Quality and freshness (S3-08):** (1) `quality` is a module without tables: it reads properties, media and agencies through their APIs and writes only the derived `quality_score` (no version bump, no event). (2) Score weights and targets are product constants in contracts (`QUALITY_COMPONENTS`), v1. (3) The quality score is owner-only (it reveals freshness); ranking across agencies will use a score without freshness when search lands. (4) Hiding is a flag set by the hourly sweep, not a time-based RLS predicate, so read models and search get an event; a listing keeps its visibility. (5) Confirmation: create, the confirm button (no `version`: idempotent), and any transition to ACTIVE (edit or bulk). Feed refreshes come with S6. (6) Photos still processing are not penalised; the job re-checks until their size is known (processing emits no event). (7) Migration 0052 updates and indexes `properties` in one transaction without `CONCURRENTLY` — acceptable pre-launch only; later migrations on large tables must batch and build indexes concurrently. (8) No notification is sent for `confirmationDue` yet (notifications module, later sprint).
- 2026-10-16 · **Listings list and bulk actions (S3-07):** (1) Bulk actions run as the member who asked (`withMemberCtx` per chunk), not `withSystem`: RLS and the policy apply exactly as for an edit, and a member who left stops their action. (2) Staff impersonating a member cannot start bulk actions (a bulk change touches status, publication and the deal at once; single edits keep the S3-02 rules). (3) A bulk price change rounds to whole units of the currency; listings without a price fail (`LISTING_PRICE_MISSING`). (4) Tags are new (`property_tags`, STRICT, internal: never shown in Client Mode); adding one bumps the listing `version` and emits `updated` with `changed: ['tags']`, like content changes (S3-05). (5) "One event per listing" is read as one `properties.listing.updated` per changed listing; status and visibility changes also emit `statusChanged` / `visibilityChanged` like an edit, so consumers see the same stream. (6) Pool `imports` (bulk listing writes), one action per agency at a time and one waiting/running per member; a lost job is failed after 2 h without progress. (7) The location filter matches the exact location, not its subtree (the repo cannot read taxonomy tables; S3-F6). (8) There are no listings in the scale seeder yet: the acceptance is measured in `tests/perf` on 200,000 seeded listings (the 1,000-agency scale) — S3-F6 adds them to `db:seed:scale`. (9) Saved views are private to the member; shared agency views can come later.
- 2026-10-15 · **Media manager (S3-06):** (1) Videos and documents are split into S3-F5: documents must not join the global content-addressed namespace (S3-03 decision 4) and need their own per-agency storage and STRICT table; videos are better as links (YouTube/Vimeo/tours) than 100 MB+ uploads — both are a design of their own, not UI. The manager handles photos and floor plans (`IMAGE`/`FLOOR_PLAN`). (2) Previews are signed GETs (1 h) of the 320 px variant, because the media bucket is not public until S3-F4's edge rule; read models and websites will use public variant URLs then. The API therefore loads `MEDIA_URL_KEY`. (3) Room types are a closed list in contracts (`LISTING_ROOM_TYPES`, 18 values) over the existing `text` column — AI tagging (later) writes the same values; no migration. (4) A cover is never unset, only passed on (`cover: true`); a cover changed into a floor plan hands it to the first image. (5) Reorder sends the full id list; any mismatch is `MEDIA_ORDER_STALE` (another tab changed the media) instead of a partial merge. (6) Media changes do not emit `properties.listing.updated` yet (only `media.object.referencesChanged` on attach/detach); the read-model task must subscribe to media order/cover changes — add an event there. (7) Duplicate skipping is client-side by hash against the listing's current media; the server still ignores an attached hash on register, so a stale page cannot double-attach. (8) The S3-04 note about re-encoding the agency logo stub stays open: this task does not touch logos.
- 2026-10-15 · **Listing editor (S3-05):** (1) Translation and feature saves bump the listing `version` and emit `properties.listing.updated` (read models rebuild on content changes); the editor holds one version and serializes its saves, so a second tab editing the same listing gets `VERSION_CONFLICT` and a reload button rather than a silent overwrite. (2) The web keeps the repo's server-action transport (`apiRequest`) instead of TanStack Query + generated SDK (frontend rules): no dashboard page uses the SDK yet; switching is one change across all pages when `pnpm sdk:generate` covers the dashboard API. (3) Locales: the editor offers every configured content locale (default first), not only the agency's `enabledLocales` — S3-08's quality score can weigh the enabled ones. (4) Field locks are edited as the S3-02 `lockedFields` list (nine lockable fields); manual edits still ignore them (S3-02 decision 7). (5) The listings section is open in Client Mode (`listing.read` is Client-Mode safe; the API strips commission and private fields); the editor opens read-only there and for deleted or other agencies' listings. (6) The list page names type and location from `/v1/taxonomy` (one call, cached); S3-07 replaces it with the real list and bulk actions.
- 2026-10-15 · **Media processing (S3-04):** (1) The original is deleted once processed: the normalized master (private, WebP q90, ≤ 2560 px) is the stored source of truth, variants are regenerated from it (PLAN §3 #33 "normalized master"); this also closes S1-F7's "stored without EXIF" check for listing media. The agency logo stub still stores its upload as is — re-encode it when the media manager UI (S3-06) touches logos. (2) Variant keys use an HMAC of the hash with a dedicated `MEDIA_URL_KEY` instead of the raw hash (S3-03 decision 3) — `v{pipeline}/{publicId}/{size}` rather than the backlog's literal `v{pipeline}/{sha}/{size}`. (3) "Byte-identical" holds for the same pipeline version and encoder stack: libvips picks SIMD code per CPU, so workers on different CPU types may encode slightly different bytes for the same key (visually identical); a unit test pins sharp/libvips/libwebp so an upgrade forces a pipeline bump. (4) WebP effort 2 (not the default 4): half the CPU for ~15 % larger files; needed for the 1.5 s budget on noisy photos. (5) Orphan cleanup deletes files before the record (S3-03 decision 2 said record first): the due record keeps every check asking for a fresh upload while files go, a failed delete is retried instead of leaking files nothing can find, and a re-use during the window resets the object to unprocessed for the reconciler. Accepted narrow race: an object re-used between its file deletion and record deletion can briefly lack its variants until reprocessed. (6) Processing failures for good: unreferenced → record dropped; referenced → `failed_at`, original deleted (EXIF), check answers UPLOAD; a fresh upload processes it again (job ID carries the event ID). (7) `requestVariants` is a system API without `ctx` (worker/read models); a route exposing it must authorize and rate-limit. (8) Security review findings deferred to S3-F4: media container still receives every worker secret (needs pool-aware config) and runs as `app_system`; public access to the media bucket must be limited to `v<n>/…` keys at the edge. (9) Throughput: ~0.9 s per 12 MP image per media process; the S3 exit criterion (10k listings with photos in < 1 h on staging) needs about (images ÷ 4,000) media processes — size the staging role accordingly (dedupe skips repeated photos).
- 2026-10-15 · **Media upload (S3-03), for S3-04 and later tasks:** (1) `media_objects` is global and keyed by the content hash (PK `sha256`, not a uuid: the hash is the identity); tenants only read it, the worker writes it (`withSystem`), so the RLS model is unchanged. `refcount` is eventually consistent (recount per event). (2) **S3-04's orphan cleanup must** lock the row (`for update`), recount `property_media` by hash itself (never trust `refcount`/`delete_after` alone), delete the row and only then the storage object; and sweep `originals/` objects ≥ 24 h old with no `media_objects` row (uploaded but never registered, or their sync event dead-lettered) — signed URLs make that unbounded until then (accepted; a per-tenant byte quota on `check` if abuse shows). A cascade delete of listings (hard purge, agency deletion) emits no event: purge jobs must emit `media.object.referencesChanged`, or the cleanup reconciles every object. (3) **S3-04 must** re-hash each original before processing (the signed checksum is enforced by MinIO; R2 to be confirmed — Handover) and never serve originals (EXIF): browsers get variants only. Public variant keys should not expose the raw SHA-256 (it links white-labelled sites to the owner's photos and lets a hash holder attach the object): derive them from an HMAC of the hash. (4) Accepted: any member who may list can learn whether a hash is stored anywhere (the dedupe the task asks for) and read its size/refcount; documents (VIDEO/DOCUMENT kinds) must not join this global namespace — a per-agency prefix and STRICT table when their task comes. (5) `mif1`/`msf1` HEIF brands are labelled `image/heic`; the decoder (S3-04) decides, in the sandboxed media worker. (6) `property_media.media_object_id` was dropped in the same release (no data existed), against expand → contract. (7) Clients set `content-length` themselves (browsers must); the other signed headers are sent as given; 412 on PUT = stored already, go on to register. (8) The "an uploaded JPEG is stored without EXIF" check (S1-F7) and the logo stub's re-encoding move to S3-04 (sharp arrives there).

- 2026-10-15 · **Staff list indexes under RLS (S2-F1):** no `(status, created_at, id)` index on `agencies`: under `app_staff` RLS the enum `=` is not leakproof, so Postgres never uses a status condition as an index condition (it stays above the policy filter). Same rule for any RLS-read list: only leakproof conditions (uuid/text/int `=`, `<`) reach an index. (2) the S0-06 perf test's `docker restart` of redis-queue-test can come back **without its published port** on Docker Desktop, after which every queue test fails to reach Redis; `restartRedisQueue()` now checks `docker port` and recreates the container (same AOF volume) when the port is missing. - 2026-10-10 · **Graceful shutdown order** (S0-08): `draining` (readiness 503) → optional `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DELAY_MS` (default 0; kamal-proxy drains on its own) → `closing` (new requests 503 with `Connection: close`) → `app.close()` waits for in-flight requests → queues/cache/db close. Worker pools get 25 s inside the 30 s process deadline, then stalled jobs are retried. Next apps rely on `next start`'s own SIGTERM handling. On Windows, SIGTERM cannot be delivered to a child process, so the boot test asserts exit 0 only on Linux; the drain itself is tested in-process.

No per-request DB check in the API; revocation = no new tokens after a password reset (`session_version`), so a stolen token lives ≤ 15 min. Web sessions re-check the user every 5 min (Auth.js `jwt` callback) and end when revoked. - 2026-10-10 · **Email confirmation needs the account password** (S0-09, security audit M1): prevents pre-account hijack (someone signs up with another person's address and the owner confirms it). Display names reject links (no `://`, dots must be followed by a space) because they appear in our emails.

- 2026-10-11 · **S1-04 two-factor authentication.**
  - **Required roles:** staff, `AGENCY_ADMIN` and `DEVELOPER_ADMIN` (PLAN §12 says "agency admins"; the developer admin has the same powers over its account). Anyone who opts in is held to it too.
  - **Enforced at the access-token mint**, not per page: every dashboard read or write needs a token, so a session that owes 2FA reaches nothing. The 2FA and security pages call identity directly (auth-flow exception, ADR 0004).
  - **Session upgrade by proof:** Auth.js hands browser-supplied data to the `jwt` callback on `update`, so the session trusts only an identity HMAC proof (2 minutes, bound to user and session version).   - The enrolment page creates the pending secret on GET (idempotent: reused until confirmed). Moving it behind a POST is in S1-F8.
  - The TOTP window stays ±1 step (clock drift); the daily per-user cap (20) bounds slow guessing to about 0.3 % a day per account (security review).
  - New dependency: qrcode 1.5.4 (+ @types/qrcode, dev) in web, for the enrolment QR code, rendered server-side as an inert `<img>` data URL.

  - **Throttle, not debounce:** the queue's `debounceMs` is trailing (the email would leave 10 minutes after the *last* login); the rate limiter gives a leading edge — the first unverified login sends at once. The sliding window means the next resend comes 10–20 minutes later.
  - **Recurring jobs** are the platform's first scheduler (S1-08's partition maintenance will use it). A renamed or removed recurring job leaves its scheduler in Redis: remove it with `removeJobScheduler` in the same change.

  - Request ids trust the configured edge header like the API; this assumes the web origin is reachable only through the edge (kamal-proxy behind Cloudflare). Locking the origin to edge traffic is an S1-F5/infra concern.
  - Code review flagged invite tokens (7-day TTL) as kept too long — they live in `agency_invites`, not `auth_tokens`; the prune now also goes by `used_at`, so "used more than 7 days ago" holds for any TTL.

- 2026-10-12 · **S1-F3 platform and core cleanups.**
  - The BEGIN round trip carries the settings by intercepting the pooled client's first `query` call for the transaction (Drizzle offers no hook before `begin`; `SET LOCAL` needs literals just the same). Values are escaped with node-pg's `escapeLiteral`; the UUID values are regex-checked before, the reasons come from code. A multi-statement simple query cannot carry bind parameters, which is why literals are used at all. Drizzle sees the combined statement as `begin`, so `countQueries` excludes it as transaction control.
  - `countQueries` is a Drizzle logger hook, not a pg wrapper: `withSystemClient` (COPY streams) is not counted, and overlapping counts see each other's statements — count one scenario at a time. Budgets are written in statements (begin/commit excluded) unless a test asks for round trips.
  - The flag reload reads as `app_user` through `withGlobalRead` (read-only, no tenant), not `app_system`: the dashboard and workers have that URL, and `feature_flags` is a global table `app_user` may read. Without a reader (unit tests, scripts) the reload falls back to the caller's transaction as before.
  - Over-cap retry backoff is per process (an in-memory map by job id, cleared when the job runs, dead-letters or releases its slot); a job that moves to another worker starts again at the first delay — bounded, and no Redis round trip per retry.
  - Review and audit outcomes (S1-F3): the BEGIN hook is an own property deleted after the transaction (a stored `.bind()` grew per transaction); the transaction fails before any statement if BEGIN was not intercepted (audit settings must never be silently absent); the pooled client is destroyed only when a control statement (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK) failed, never for an error thrown by `fn`; `withSystem`/`withStaff` refuse NUL in reasons; pools pin `client_encoding: 'UTF8'` (the only encoding under which `escapeLiteral` is byte-safe); flag reads serve an expired snapshot while the reload runs or fails (stale-while-revalidate), so a saturated `app_user` pool cannot stall requests at the 60-second expiry; the generated policy test asserts every `CLIENT_MODE_ALLOWED` entry is a read action.
- 2026-10-12 · **S1-F2 outbox hardening.**
  - A lane claims again without a pause after *any* non-empty batch, not only a full one (ADR 0014 says "while batches are full"): a fair batch is cut by rounding and a trickle of small agencies can leave it under-full while rows are still due. An idle lane still costs one index probe per 250 ms.
  - The fair claim serves at most `maxAgenciesPerClaim` = 64 agencies per claim (each costs an enumeration probe, a count probe and a locking scan: 600 agencies with backlog measured 157 ms per claim uncapped, far over the 20 ms SQL budget) and rotates a per-lane cursor across claims, so every due agency is reached within ⌈agencies / 64⌉ claims — with 5,000 agencies all importing at once, under 80 claims, i.e. a few seconds, instead of one batch. Lanes keep independent cursors; `SKIP LOCKED` keeps them off each other's rows.
  - `outbox_events_pending_idx` now leads with `agency_id`. There is no longer an index ordered by `available_at` alone: nothing reads the oldest pending row globally (replay is by `id`; a future "oldest pending event age" metric would group by agency or add its own index).
  - Autovacuum settings for `outbox_events` are a custom migration (0030: vacuum at 1 % / 5,000 dead rows, insert-vacuum at 5 % / 10,000, analyze at 2 % / 5,000, cost delay 1 ms). No `fillfactor`: the claim and the acknowledgement both change indexed columns, so updates are not HOT anyway.
  - Delivery stays tracked per event (one `processed_at`), and PATTERNS §8 / workers.md now require each subscriber to be idempotent on its own, instead of a per-subscriber delivery table. Subscribers already enqueue jobs with stable IDs; the extra table would add a write per subscriber per event on the hottest path for a guarantee consumers must not rely on anyway (at-least-once).
  - Code review (S1-F2): the first cut counted due rows per agency up to `batchSize` — O(agencies × min(backlog, 500)), measured 221–339 ms (1.5 s cold) for 600 agencies × 200 rows. The probe now stops at the equal share `ceil(batchSize / agencies)`; agencies at the share are recounted up to the level the small ones leave them (a one-pass cap under-filled a 50 k burst + 107 platform rows + 46 small agencies to 356 of 500); the water level comes from the first agency at or above its probe limit. A big agency with fewer rows than a level raised twice can still leave slots empty in that batch; the lane claims again at once.
  - Security audit (S1-F2): the pg_hba rules and the ufw rule that let app hosts and the `kamal` network reach Postgres 5432 directly as `app_system` existed only for LISTEN; both are removed, so a compromised app host can reach the database only through PgBouncer (`127.0.0.1`). Migration 0029 rebuilds the pending index non-concurrently (fine before launch; a live system would need a `CONCURRENTLY` out-of-transaction migration).
  - `pnpm verify` (9 min, 58 tasks) had one failure on this machine: `tests/isolation/guard.int.test.ts` lost its `applyRls` lock-timeout race (`set local lock_timeout = '5s'`, "canceling statement due to lock timeout") while the queue and perf suites were hammering `outbox_events` in parallel. `pnpm test:isolation` alone passes (342 tests). Watch for a repeat; if it recurs, make `test:isolation` depend on `test:int:root` / `test:perf:root` in turbo.json so the ALTER TABLE statements never compete with the outbox load.
  - Two `pnpm verify` runs on this machine ended on unrelated Windows flakes: a Vitest fork worker of `@inmolink/app-api` `test:int` died with 0xC0000409 (the crash the vitest config already works around for the root projects with `pool: 'threads'`) and, once, the isolation guard's `applyRls` lock timeout above. Each suite passes when re-run alone. Tried `pool: 'threads'` in the shared Vitest preset: the core int suite's main process then died with 0xC0000409 twice under `verify` (a native-module crash in a worker thread takes the whole run down; forks are isolated), so forks stay and `pnpm verify` caps Turbo at `--concurrency=4` instead; `test:isolation` now depends on every package's int suite so `applyRls` never competes with them.
  - The throughput perf test keeps its `[S0-06]` tag and its ≥ 2,000 events/s check (ADR 0014 keeps it); the `restartRedisQueue` helper's `docker compose up --force-recreate` can fail on Docker Desktop for Windows (the container stays `Created`): start `redis-queue-test` by hand and re-run.
- 2026-10-12 · **S1-10 dashboard shell.**
  - Capabilities live in a core module of their own (`modules/dashboard`), not in identity: the aggregator imports every module's `index.ts`, so putting it in identity would have made the lowest module depend on the ones above it. Modules that add a dashboard section register it there (PATTERNS: a module without tables is fine; it has no repo or schema).
  - `identity.members.read` is now refused in Client Mode (S1-02 policy change): the member roster (names, emails, roles) is internal data, like the partner list (`agencies.preferred.read`). Client Mode is still hard-wired off (`core/member.ts`), so nothing changes for users yet; the dashboard hides the Team section once it is live.
  - The web mints one api token per render and audience and asks `/v1/staff/me` once per render (React `cache` keyed by primitives): the shell, the layout and the page share them. Before, a staff console page minted three times and called the staff API twice.
  - `lighthouse` 13.5.0 is a root devDependency, used only by `tests/e2e/shell.spec.ts` (the accessibility acceptance check; the same tool measures the public pages' Lighthouse ≥ 90 later). It drives a second Playwright Chromium (`channel: 'chromium'`, DevTools on `PORTS.devtools`) and sends the session cookie as an extra header — fine while the dashboard loads only same-origin assets; switch to CDP `Network.setCookie` if a third-party script is ever embedded.
  - `pnpm perf:bundle` reads `.next/build-manifest.json` and the per-route `page_client-reference-manifest.js` files without evaluating them (Next 16 Turbopack prints no first-load sizes). CI runs it with `--if-present` because PR runs build only affected apps.
  - The e2e TOTP helper now tries the current step first, then the next, then the previous (it used to start with the previous step and lost a code computed just before a 30-second boundary: one password-reset run failed that way).

- 2026-10-14 · **S1-F6 database and Redis operations.**
  - **Rate limits on redis-queue, not a third Redis:** the task offered redis-queue with a prefix or a `volatile-lru` split; `volatile-lru` would still evict counters (they carry TTLs), so redis-queue it is. Production connects as an ACL user confined to `inl:rl:*`; the test runs the real limiter as that user.
  - **Residual risks (security review), accepted for now:** (1) redis-queue has no `maxmemory`: a flood of distinct identities creates counter keys (each lives ≤ 2 windows) in the Redis that also holds jobs — add memory and `inl:rl:*` key-count alerts with the monitoring dashboards; a `maxmemory` cap would fail BullMQ writes too. (2) All apps share the `inl:rl:*` prefix, so a compromised feed-api could reset web's login counters; per-app prefixes and users if that matters. (3) api still holds the full `REDIS_QUEUE_URL` (it enqueues); a producer ACL user is a later hardening. (4) The limiter now shares a single-threaded Redis with BullMQ: a latency spike over 200 ms fails closed on `auth.*` rules — watch the limiter's fail-closed warnings.
  - **max_db_connections is per database, shared by every role:** long app_system work can still starve request roles, which now get a fast error instead of a 120 s hang. Per-role pool sizes when Stage B splits workers out.
  - **Users-phase budget:** the perf test asserts 15.2 s / 5 = 3.04 s, the review's figure; on this machine the old code took 6.1 s, so the same-machine speed-up is 3.2–4.7×. The 15.2 s figure came from an earlier, slower environment.

- 2026-10-14 · **S1-F7 verification follow-ups.**
  - **Image re-encoding and the scan hook move to S3-03** (sharp arrives with the media pipeline; adding sharp now would be a heavy dependency ahead of its task). Acceptance check "an uploaded JPEG is stored without EXIF" is open and belongs to S3-03; verification images stay attachment-only downloads for staff until then.
  - **Dedupe, not `Idempotency-Key`:** the task allowed either; `(agency_id, sha256)` among unsubmitted documents needs no client change and no key store.
  - **Sweeper bound:** at most 200 pages × 500 objects per prefix per run, always from the start of the prefix; past ~100k objects per prefix it needs a persisted cursor (revisit in S3-03 with the media bucket).
  - **Staff `users.status`:** `app_staff` cannot read `users`, so `withStaffCtx` does one extra short `app_auth` read per staff request (staff traffic is low). Nothing sets `DISABLED` yet; the check is ready for when something does.

Before the first COPY path, add `withTenantClient(scope, fn)` / `withSystemClient(reason, fn)`, which wrap begin/commit/rollback and destroy the client on error.
